name: chitin
summary: The shell an insect or an arachnid is made of: a hard plate over a body, darker and harder than flesh and not made by anybody.
why: The library names what a thing is made of, and a spider is not made of any of the
twenty-four things already in it. It is not skin, which is what a first pass reaches for
because both are on a living body: skin scatters and gives almost nothing back, and a
carapace is a hard shell that catches a highlight along its curve. It is not leather
either, which is the other tempting answer - leather is a hide that has been tanned flat
by somebody, and it declares a weave along u for the cord it is wound as.
Metallic 0.0. Obvious, and worth writing down anyway: every organic surface in this
library is dielectric, and an unnamed slot inheriting an armour default is the single
way a monster turns into a chrome statue of itself.
Roughness 0.62, between hair's 0.62 and skin's 0.78 and deliberately not skin's. A shell
is the one part of a creature that is genuinely a little glossy, and the whole reason to
have this material rather than reuse skin is that it says so. It is not taken lower than
this: skin.json records that 0.55 on a body caught a broad highlight reading as a
mannequin's shine, and MU has already painted its own shading into the sheet, so a strong
specular laid on top is a second light the artist never drew. A spider is small and dark
and seen from above; the honest amount of shine at that size is a little, not a lot.
No grain, and for the same reason skin has none. The three kinds this pipeline has -
brushed, weave, cast - are each a fact about how a surface was made, and a real carapace
does have a fine pitting that would be a cast grain if anything could resolve it. Nothing
can: the Spider's whole body is a 64x64 sheet and its legs are 32x64, so a pit is far
smaller than a texel and any grain here would be invented rather than reconstructed.
The hair is on these sheets too and is not split off, which is the opposite of what
HelmClass02 wanted. A spider's bristles are painted into the alpha of the leg sheet as
part of the silhouette rather than laid out as their own island - the legs are seventy-two
triangles in one group - so there is no geometry to give a second material to. See
hair.json for the case where there was.
